title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is grappling with supply chain vulnerabilities while also pushing forward with ambitious projects like microgravity flight testing and tactical satellite constellations. Meanwhile, the budgetary landscape is shifting, with increased funding aimed at enhancing space resilience.

themes.title: Supply Chain Concerns Persist
themes.body: A report highlights the U.S. space supply chains' heavy reliance on Chinese manufacturing, raising red flags about future operational stability. As geopolitical tensions simmer, expect calls for domestic production to intensify.

themes.title: Microgravity Testing Gains Traction
themes.body: Sierra Space and Starfighters are ramping up efforts in microgravity flight testing, signaling a renewed focus on experimental capabilities. This could pave the way for more innovative applications in low Earth orbit.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space. This funding could bolster efforts against emerging threats, particularly in satellite operations.

themes.title: Defense-Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window is showing signs of life, with several companies eyeing public offerings. This could reshape the investment landscape, drawing more capital into the space sector as it matures.
